# Abandoned, not forgotten

> An interactive story about the machines NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars: the ALSEP science stations, the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages and the Sojourner rover — what they were built for, what they found, and what still remains there today.

## The three main machines

- [ALSEP](https://YOUR-SITE.vercel.app/): Five nuclear-powered science stations deployed by Apollo 12-17 astronauts. Powered by SNAP-27 radioisotope generators, they ran moonquake, heat-flow and solar-wind experiments. NASA switched them off on 30 September 1977; they are still on the Moon.
- [Lunar Module descent stage](https://YOUR-SITE.vercel.app/): The landing pad that became a launch pad. Apollo 12's Intrepid descent stage still sits in the Ocean of Storms at 3.01S 23.42W, beside Surveyor Crater.
- [Sojourner](https://YOUR-SITE.vercel.app/): Mars Pathfinder's rover, built for a 7-sol mission. It worked for 83 sols and drove about 100 metres, and is still parked in Ares Vallis, now part of the Carl Sagan Memorial Station.

## More left behind

- On the Moon: five ALSEP stations, six Apollo Lunar Module descent stages, three Lunar Roving Vehicles, and other equipment.
- On Mars: Viking 1 and Viking 2 landers, Spirit and Opportunity rovers, Phoenix and InSight landers, and more.

## About

Made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by NASA. Map positions are approximate.
